enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing scope is not a least-privilege request on authentik; tests must request explicit minimal scopes.

oidc_jwt.description: The email_verified claim defaults to false unless customized by a scope mapping.
oidc_jwt.note: Applications expecting email_verified=true may fail by design unless a custom mapping is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: In machine-to-machine authentication, authentik treats grant_type=password the same as client_credentials.
oidc_jwt.note: Success on password grant in this context is compatibility behavior, not evidence of end-user password grant support.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive a refresh token when both the request and provider configuration include offline_access.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is configured and requested.

oidc_jwt.description: For machine-to-machine authentication, authentik treats grant_type=password the same as client_credentials.
oidc_jwt.note: Password-grant behavior here is a compatibility feature, not necessarily end-user ROPC semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT authentication creates service accounts based on provider name and token subject, and these may expire based on the input token exp claim.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity material returned for JWT auth may represent generated service accounts rather than pre-existing human users.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-authentication documentation only states signature and expiry checks for external JWTs and does not document jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of the same stateless JWT more than once may be by design unless additional policy or revocation checks apply.

oidc_jwt.description: If the OAuth2 provider Redirect URI field is empty, the first URL used to open the app is saved as the redirect URL.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs
oidc_jwt.note: This can make an initial unexpected redirect URI succeed by design during setup.

oidc_jwt.description: OAuth source discovery metadata is fetched when the source is saved and is not automatically re-fetched later.
oidc_jwt.note: Stale discovery/JWKS behavior after upstream changes may reflect cached configuration until the source is saved again.

oidc_jwt.description: Service accounts created from JWT authentication expire and are deleted based on the expiry claim of the input token, if set.
oidc_jwt.note: Disappearance of identities after token expiry can be expected cleanup behavior, not identity corruption.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT client_assertion as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation only states that input JWTs must be signed by configured sources/providers and not expired/revoked; it does not document jti tracking or one-time-use enforcement for generic JWT authentication.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, the input JWT MUST include exp in the future for the control case (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}) and exp in the past for the attack case (for example exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}}). authentik explicitly checks that external JWT exp is not now or in the past, and authentik-issued JWTs must not have expired.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests, the documentation does not explicitly state whether nbf is validated for JWT client assertions. The fuzzer SHOULD run a valid control token alongside the attack token and interpret failures cautiously; only exp validation is explicitly documented.

For I1 resign_attacker_key and kid_injection tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST select the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s) whose JWKS/certificates are trusted. Without that trust configuration, login failures are not evidence of correct signature validation; they may simply reflect missing trust setup.

For I1 trust_anchor_substitution tests, when using external JWTs, the fuzzer MUST configure a source with Well-known URL, OIDC JWKS URL, or raw JWKS data first. authentik fetches discovery/JWKS data on save and uses the configured source certificates as trust anchors. A forged issuer with attacker JWKS is only meaningful if the provider under test is configured to trust a different source.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik does not document a built-in issuer binding parameter for JWT client assertion authentication. Issuer restrictions, if desired, are implemented via Expression policies using request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. Therefore, the fuzzer MUST create and bind an expression policy that checks iss; otherwise issuer-mismatch tests are inconclusive because no issuer comparison was configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, the documentation does not state that the input JWT aud claim is validated during JWT client assertion authentication. The fuzzer MUST use an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"] to enforce aud if it wants a deterministic audience-binding oracle; otherwise cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance may be by design for this feature.

For I5 scope tests, when no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST explicitly request a minimal scope set when testing scope escalation or claim over-issuance; omitting scope broadens claims by design and will cause false positives.

For refresh-token-related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 a refresh token is only issued when both the application/provider configuration includes offline_access and the request explicitly asks for offline_access. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a bug unless both conditions are satisfied.

For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer MUST use the same code twice to test replay rejection, and MUST distinguish this from legitimate expiry by running the replay immediately after a successful baseline exchange.

For I3 config-change sequences involving JWT trust rotation, authentik states that JWT trust comes from configured Federated OIDC Sources/Providers and fetched JWKS data stored in the source on save. A valid key-rotation test MUST update the source/provider trust configuration and then perform a NEW login_with_jwt. Do NOT compare outcomes of requests issued before the configuration change.

For I3 default-role/default-binding analogs, authentik's JWT authentication is tied to the OAuth2 provider and selected federated sources/providers rather than a Vault-style role parameter. The fuzzer MUST model config-change tests around provider/source selection and bound expression policies, not around a non-existent role field.

For OIDC request object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), start_oidc_auth supports the optional request parameter. The executor MUST send it as a query parameter to /application/o/authorize/ and MUST NOT follow redirects automatically. A non-200/redirect outcome should be evaluated at the authorization endpoint itself.

For OIDC code-flow tests, redirect_uri matching is security-relevant. authentik documents that redirect URIs are validated against the provider configuration, and the field may be empty on first use or may contain regexes. The fuzzer MUST know whether the provider is configured with an explicit URI, empty first-use capture, or regex; otherwise redirect_uri_mismatch results may be misinterpreted.

Redirect URI configuration in authentik may use regular expressions rather than exact string matching. Therefore, for redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST avoid broad regex configurations unless intentionally testing regex behavior. A regex-configured provider can legitimately accept multiple redirect URIs.

For OIDC PKCE tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded data. If code_verifier is omitted, any rejection should be interpreted via HTTP status/error response, not identity comparison.

For OIDC id_token validation constraints when authentik acts as RP via OAuth sources, the documentation states that discovery/JWKS URLs are configured and fetched on save, but does not explicitly enumerate nonce/aud/iss/exp validation behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD test these checks empirically and MUST include a valid control flow for each attack case to avoid false positives from generic source misconfiguration.

For cross-provider JWT audience tests, authentik allows an OAuth2 provider to trust one or more Federated OIDC Sources or Providers for JWT authentication. The fuzzer MUST create distinct providers and ensure the attack token is minted for provider-A while being presented to provider-B. Because aud enforcement is not explicitly documented for JWT authentication, acceptance is only a vulnerability if a policy or documented provider restriction was configured to require audience binding.

For token introspection, authentik documents that you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, unless you first exchange the token for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST introspect with matching provider credentials or perform a prior token exchange; otherwise introspection failure is expected by design.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, authentik explicitly checks only that externally issued input JWTs are signed by a configured federated OIDC source and that exp is not now or in the past. The docs do not state validation of nbf, iat, iss, aud, or jti for this JWT-authentication path. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid JWT alongside any attack token and MUST treat missing rejection of nbf/future-token or replay as potentially by-design unless separately enforced by policy.

For I1 trust-anchor and signature tests, login_with_jwt only works after the target OAuth2 provider is configured to trust either selected Federated OIDC Sources (external JWKS) or Federated OIDC Providers (authentik-issued JWTs). Without that trust configuration, failures are setup failures, not proof-validation results.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation shows issuer restriction only via optional Expression policies using request.context['oauth_jwt']. Omitting such a policy means issuer comparison is not documented as enforced for JWT-authentication. The fuzzer MUST add an expression policy that checks oauth_jwt['iss'] when testing issuer binding; otherwise acceptance of a forged issuer is inconclusive.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, the documentation does not describe a built-in audience restriction parameter for JWT-authentication. Access can be dynamically limited only with Expression policies over request.context['oauth_jwt']. The fuzzer MUST enforce aud in policy when testing audience mismatch; otherwise cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance may reflect missing configuration rather than a validation bug.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, when a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope value in token and authorization requests. Omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.

For refresh-token and offline-access scenarios, starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive a refresh token when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the request includes offline_access. The fuzzer MUST configure and request offline_access together; otherwise absence of refresh_token is by design.

For I3 config-change sequences, authentik states that OAuth sources fetch OIDC discovery metadata only when the source is saved and do not automatically re-fetch it. After changing a Well-known URL or upstream JWKS/discovery-backed source configuration, the fuzzer MUST perform the documented save/update action before expecting new trust settings to apply.

For I3 source-stage and external-source flow tests, the Source stage suspends the current flow and resumes it later, but if the source's authentication or enrollment flow contains a User Login stage, the original flow will not resume and the pending user is directly authenticated. The fuzzer MUST avoid treating this as session confusion; it is a documented misconfiguration hazard.

For OIDC redirect_uri tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider's configured Redirect URI list. If the Redirect URI field is left empty when creating a new OAuth2 provider, authentik saves the first URL used to open the app as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST explicitly configure redirect URIs before mismatch tests; otherwise first-use auto-registration can mask redirect validation behavior.

Redirect URI matching supports regular expressions when configured by the administrator. The fuzzer MUST distinguish exact redirect URI entries from regex-based entries. A permissive regex can intentionally allow multiple callbacks and is not evidence of redirect_uri validation failure.

For OIDC request-object alg_none testing, start_oidc_auth may include a request JWT via the request parameter, but the documentation provided does not describe request-object signature enforcement settings. The fuzzer SHOULD test unsigned request objects, but any acceptance must be interpreted cautiously unless the provider/client is documented as requiring signed request objects.

For OIDC RP validation tests where authentik acts as a relying party to external OAuth/OIDC sources, the docs describe configuring Authorization URL, Access Token URL, Profile URL, and OIDC JWKS URL, and note that login_hint may be sent. The docs do not explicitly document nonce, aud, iss, or exp validation of upstream id_tokens in this excerpt. The fuzzer MUST use control logins and SHOULD not assume these checks are configurable unless documented on the source.

For I4 identity-collision tests on JWT-authentication, authentik creates service accounts based on the provider name and the subject claim of the input token. Cross-provider collisions are therefore expected to be separated by provider name in the generated service-account naming scheme. The fuzzer MUST compare identities across providers with provider context included.

For I4 replay/collision tests involving externally issued JWTs, authentik may create multiple service accounts depending on the tokens provided, and those service accounts expire and are deleted based on the exp claim if set. The fuzzer MUST not assume persistence of identities after token expiry.

For I5 token introspection tests, authentik documentation states you are only able to introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or you must first exchange the token for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests in the same provider context or perform token exchange first; cross-provider introspection failures are by design.

For token exchange and cross-provider federation tests, authentik-issued JWT authentication requires the input JWT to be a valid access token issued by one of the configured Federated OIDC Providers, and it must not have been revoked or expired. The fuzzer MUST use access_token as subject/input token, not id_token.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, authentik exposes requested scopes to expression policies via request.context['oauth_scopes'] and by default every user with access to an application can request any configured scopes. The fuzzer MUST bind an expression policy to the application/provider to restrict sensitive scopes; otherwise expanded scopes are by design if they are configured on the provider.

For I5 claim-surface tests, values returned by OAuth2 scope mappings are added as custom claims to access and ID tokens. The fuzzer MUST account for scope mappings as the source of claims; unexpected claims may come from configured mappings rather than unauthorized token broadening.

Numeric sentinel: User Login stage Session duration uses seconds=0 as a special value meaning the authentik session expires when the browser is closed, not a literal already-expired session. Stay signed in offset also defaults to seconds=0 meaning no extension prompt. Never interpret 0 as disable-authentication or immediate invalidation.

Numeric sentinel: Authenticator Validation stage Last validation threshold uses non-zero to reduce MFA frequency; values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used reliably for code-based devices because exact timestamps are not available. The fuzzer MUST avoid sub-30-second thresholds for TOTP/static/SMS freshness tests.

Numeric sentinel: Email Authenticator Setup stage Token Expiration is in minutes with default 30. The fuzzer MUST not assume 0 disables expiry unless explicitly documented; no such disable sentinel is documented here.

For JWT login tests, authentik's documented JWT authentication path is POST /application/o/token/ with grant_type=client_credentials and client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer plus client_assertion=<JWT>. The fuzzer MUST NOT use an invented dedicated JWT login endpoint.

authentik also accepts the input JWT in client_secret for compatibility. This is an alternate input path, not a different validation mode. I1 tests should exercise both client_assertion and client_secret forms because middleware or parsers may treat them differently.

For externally issued JWT authentication, authentik documentation only guarantees verification that the JWT is signed by any selected Federated OIDC Source key and that exp is not now or in the past. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume issuer, audience, subject, nonce, nbf, or iat are enforced unless additional policy/config explicitly adds those checks.

For authentik-issued JWT federation, input JWTs must be valid access tokens issued by configured Federated OIDC Providers, must not have been revoked, and must not have expired. I3 key-rotation and revocation tests should use authentik-issued subject tokens when testing revocation-sensitive behavior; externally issued JWTs are documented only with signature+exp checks.

For I1 trust_anchor_substitution and resign_attacker_key tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST select the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s). Without that trust configuration, login failure is ambiguous and does not prove signature validation behavior.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against JWT M2M auth, authentik does not document a built-in issuer binding field. The documented way to restrict issuer is an Expression policy using request.context['oauth_jwt']['iss']. The fuzzer MUST add such a policy if it wants issuer enforcement to be part of the oracle; otherwise acceptance of a wrong iss is by current documented configuration, not necessarily a bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests on JWT M2M auth, authentik documentation does not state that the input JWT aud is checked during external JWT authentication. The fuzzer MUST treat audience enforcement as policy-dependent unless it configures an explicit Expression policy over request.context['oauth_jwt']['aud'].

For I2 expired_token tests, use a control JWT with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and a matching attack JWT with exp={{now_epoch_minus_60}}. authentik explicitly documents exp enforcement for external JWTs; without a valid control token, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust configuration.

For I2 future_token and nbf tests, authentik documentation does not explicitly state nbf or iat validation for external JWT authentication. The fuzzer SHOULD test these claims, but MUST classify acceptance cautiously unless explicit policy/config was added to enforce them.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti, authentik documentation does not describe jti tracking for JWT bearer M2M authentication. Reuse of the same external JWT is therefore a hardening observation at most, not a vulnerability by itself.

Machine-to-machine authentication treats grant_type=password the same as client_credentials. The fuzzer MUST recognize that password-grant success here is by design compatibility behavior, not evidence of end-user password ROPC semantics.

When no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. For I5 scope-minimization tests, the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope parameter; omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.

Starting with authentik 2024.2, refresh tokens are only returned when both the application and authentik are configured for offline_access and the request includes offline_access. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect refresh_token in generic token responses unless offline_access is explicitly configured and requested.

The authorization code can only be used once and expires quickly. For I3 code-reuse or code-injection tests, a second successful redemption would be meaningful; a second failure is expected by design.

Redirect URI validation supports exact redirect URIs and regex patterns configured by the administrator. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the provider was configured with a literal URI or a regex. A regex match is by design and not a bypass.

When the provider Redirect URI field is left empty, authentik saves the first URL a user opens for that app as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure redirect URIs explicitly before redirect_uri security tests; otherwise first-use auto-save can mask or alter expected validation behavior.

For OIDC request object alg=none tests, use the authorization endpoint /application/o/authorize/ with the request parameter. The docs state authentik follows the OIDC spec, but do not document request-object signature configuration details. The fuzzer SHOULD test unsigned request objects directly and judge by endpoint acceptance/rejection.

For verify_granted_identity, session_token MUST be the access_token, not the id_token. authentik's userinfo endpoint is an OAuth-protected API endpoint and the docs define access_token as the bearer credential for protected APIs.

The introspection endpoint can only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST keep provider context aligned during introspection tests or perform token exchange first.

For cross-provider JWT audience tests, create two OAuth2 providers and use a JWT intended for provider A against provider B. Because authentik supports federation between providers, the fuzzer MUST ensure the providers are distinct and that the subject token/provider trust relationship is configured exactly as intended; otherwise cross-provider acceptance may be expected federation behavior rather than an audience bug.

For token_exchange and cross-provider federation tests, authentik documentation says federation is enabled by selecting the provider of the application to which you want to federate. The fuzzer MUST model this as explicit trust configuration. Acceptance across providers without such configuration would be suspicious; acceptance with it may be by design depending on audience/scope handling.

For I5 scope escalation tests on exchanged or newly issued tokens, compare returned claims against explicitly requested scopes. Since authentik defaults missing scope to all configured scopes, a missing-scope request is not a valid least-privilege baseline.

For OIDC SSO validation tests where authentik acts as RP via OAuth Source, discovery or JWKS URLs are fetched and stored on save, and no automatic re-fetching is done. I3 key-rotation tests against upstream IdPs MUST account for this: changing upstream keys alone may not affect authentik until the source is re-saved/refreshed.

For OIDC SSO id_token validation tests against authentik as RP, the docs describe OAuth Source as expecting OpenID-Connect compatible information and support discovery/JWKS, but do not explicitly enumerate nonce/aud/iss/exp checks. The fuzzer SHOULD test these checks directly and MUST avoid assuming either strict validation or absence of validation from docs alone.

For Entra ID machine-to-machine JWT acquisition used as input to authentik, the upstream scope must be the Application ID URI (api://<application_client_id>/.default), not the Graph URL, or the JWT format will be invalid before it reaches authentik. The fuzzer MUST use the documented upstream scope to avoid false negatives.

Known numeric sentinel: User Login stage Session duration default seconds=0 means browser-session cookie expiry, not immediate invalidation. Stay signed in offset default seconds=0 means no extension prompt. Remember device only activates when duration is above 0. Never assume 0 disables the underlying login stage; it selects session-cookie/default behavior.

Known numeric sentinel: Authenticator Validation stage Last validation threshold only changes behavior when set to a non-zero value. Value 0 means validate every time; it does not disable MFA entirely. For code-based devices, values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used precisely.

Known numeric sentinel: Email Authenticator Setup stage Token Expiration default is 30 minutes. The docs do not define 0 as disable or immediate expiry. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 has special semantics unless verified separately.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
